title: feat(pm): close the mailboxes to outsiders — lock each mailbox PR and count a knock only from the fleet or a maintainer
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi99Z1mjGd2zxMaR5rH5Z1Ada)_
Part of #33789
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:信箱 PR 开出后立刻锁定讨论(只有有写权限的账号能评论),旧信箱可用 `--lock N` 补锁;每次锁定后中继立即在信箱发一条自检评论,发不出就自动解锁并报错;读敲门的工具只认车队机器人与维护者账号,其余作者一律忽略、正文不读。
- 为什么改:仓库公开,任何 GitHub 用户都能在信箱下留一条伪造的敲门,白白进入座位会话、耗 token;本卡把「作者决定性质」从规则变成硬闸。
- 风险与回滚:锁定后车队机器人能否继续评论尚未实测,但每次锁定都由自检评论当场实测,失败即解锁,不会留下收不到敲门的信箱;中继只对带 pm:mailbox 的开放 PR 加锁或解锁。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`scripts/pm/mailbox-open.mjs` 的 `lockStroke` / `canaryStroke`;`scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs` 的 `mailboxLockPreflight`;`scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` 的 `readMailboxComment`。
- 两分钟验证:`node scripts/pm/mailbox-open.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --lock 32588 --dry-run`,应看到一个 `conversation_lock` 动作、不发任何请求。
- 需要你做的:受管面(`.claude/**`)PR,等 GOVERNED_APPROVERS 批准或席位达档复核;合并后由席位跑一次补锁所有已开信箱的中继扫射。

## What changes

Items 1 and 2 of the card land here; item 3 (the knock's session must match the named seat's post or mailbox opening) is left open, so this PR is `Part of` the card. What item 3 needs is under Acceptance notes.

**Item 1 — the mailbox conversation is locked.**

- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs`: two new relay rows.
  - `conversation_lock` takes `issue` alone and becomes ONE `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/lock` whose body is the table's one reason, `{ lock_reason: 'resolved' }` (`CONVERSATION_LOCK_REASON`). The caller cannot send a reason.
  - `conversation_unlock` takes `issue` alone and becomes ONE `DELETE` of the same path, with no body. It exists so that a lock is never one-way (see the canary below).
  - GitHub's server-to-server permission ledger (`github/docs` `src/github-apps/data/fpt-2022-11-28/server-to-server-permissions.json`, read 2026-11-15) lists the endpoint under `issues: write` and again under `pull_requests: write`. Both are literal grants on every stroke, so both rows spend `issues` and `.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml` is untouched.
- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs` (review S2): the executor fences both rows on its own `GET` of the pull, the last read before the write, as it fences `mailbox_branch_delete`. It refuses with nothing sent unless the number is a pull request (an issue's number answers 404 on the pulls path), the pull is open, and it carries `pm:mailbox`. Each row lands only when the issue reads back with `locked` as asked. A write the platform refused whose conversation already reads that way is an idempotent landing; any other read is FAILED.
- `scripts/pm/mailbox-open.mjs`:
  - The open gains step ⑤. Once ④ has read the new pull's number back, a second relay stroke sends `conversation_lock` on that number, and the pull is then read back `locked: true`. The lock cannot ride the `pr_create` stroke because an action names its pull by number, and the number exists only after the create answers.
  - A lock that fails leaves the mailbox open and unlocked. The open then exits non-zero and names the one re-send.
  - The canary (review S1). Once the pull reads back locked, a third relay stroke posts ONE comment on it: `MAILBOX_LOCK_CANARY` above the bare footer. The relay reads it back byte for byte. If the canary is refused, a fourth stroke sends `conversation_unlock`, the pull is read back unlocked, and the run exits 3 with a loud line: the lock was taken back, and no other mailbox is locked until the refusal is understood. If the unlock fails too, the line says the mailbox may stay locked and names the maintainer's "Unlock conversation".
  - Shape chosen: the canary is a fixed line, not a doorbell key (it opens with no `To:`). Its time stamp is the comment's own `created_at`, so the line carries no clock of its own. It rides its own stroke rather than the lock's, so a refusal is read as the canary's alone and the unlock is sent only for a lock that read back.
  - `--lock N` locks a mailbox opened before this change, with the same canary. It is the one spelling the post-merge sweep uses. It reads the pull first and refuses (exit 4) unless the pull is an open `pm:mailbox` PR, the same read `--close` makes. A pull that already reads `locked` costs zero writes and gets no canary.

**Item 2 — a knock counts only from the fleet bot or a maintainer.**

- `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`: `readMailboxComment(row)` fences the doorbell on the comment's author. A knock is read only when `user.login` is in `MAILBOX_KNOCK_AUTHORS`, which is `[RELAY_COMMENT_AUTHOR, ...GOVERNED_APPROVERS]`. It is judged by the queue guard's own predicate `recordAuthorTrusted`, and no login is typed here. Any other row reads exactly `{ state: 'ignored', reason: 'ignored: not a fleet or maintainer author' }`, and its body is never handed to the parser, so no line, key or seat of it can be echoed.
- `mailboxEvents` lists ignored rows apart, as `ignored` with comment id, time and author only. They are never an event or a half-state, so check-half-states H72 does not list them (pinned end to end).
- `--mailbox-keys` prints who may ring.
- The relay's lock canary (the line alone above footer lines, one leading signature line allowed) reads `{ state: 'canary' }`. It is never an event and never a half-state, so H72 does not list it; `mailboxEvents` lists it apart as `canaries`. The same line from a maintainer, with a second line, or under a `To:` line reads as before.
- Import edge: `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` imports nothing of this graph at module scope, so the new static edge adds no cycle. Measured: the queue guard, post-stamped and recognisers self-tests pass, and `check-half-states.mjs` and `check-handover.mjs` load.

**Skill text (governed, `.claude/**`)**: one line each. The pm-dispatch ratchet is paid by deletions in the same files:

| File | Line added | Line deleted | Where the deleted rule still lives | Lines before → after |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `references/untrusted-text.md` | mailboxes are locked; a knock counts only from `objectstack-fleet[bot]` and `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` | the pointer that an adopted fork diff's internal PR waits for the maintainer's own approval | `references/external-contributions.md` ③ (lines 13–14, the rule itself) | 54 → 54 |
| `references/seat-post-protocol.md` | knocks are judged on the author field like audit and claim comments (`readMailboxComment`) | the back-pointer sentence "见 seat-lifecycle.md 〈座位贴协议〉…" and the blank line under it | `references/seat-lifecycle.md:23` points to this file itself; other references name it by purpose | 88 → 87 |

## Tests

Every number below was read at head 5fca76d4, after the last commit (round 1, review S1 and S2).

- `node scripts/pm/mailbox-open.mjs --self-test`: 103 cases in 11 batteries pass (was 90 in 10 before this PR). The battery "the lock" pins the one `conversation_lock` action the relay validator accepts, ⭐ the PUT the relay sends from it with the pull handed to the relay's fence, the open-mailbox read it runs behind, the `--lock` arguments, the re-send line and the open plan's step ⑤. Round 1 adds: ⭐ the canary is ONE relay comment, its first line `MAILBOX_LOCK_CANARY`, then the bare footer, accepted by the validator; ⛔ it is no doorbell key; ⭐ the unlock is one `conversation_unlock` and the DELETE the relay sends from it; the canary-failure line in both variants (taken back, or a maintainer's hand); and the `--lock` plan's canary step. The CLI battery has the `--lock` dry run with no gh or git on PATH.
- `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs --self-test`: 435 cases across 23 batteries pass (was 428 across 22). The lock battery now covers both rows: closed keys (a caller-sent `lock_reason` refused), ⭐ the action shape each sends, issues write as a literal grant, and exactly two ops naming a lock, each request carrying the executor's fence.
- `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs --self-test`: 423 cases across 31 batteries pass (was 415 across 30). New battery "the mailbox conversation lock": ⭐ lock and unlock each read the pull, send one write under the App token and read the issue back. ⛔ An issue's number, a closed pull, an unlabelled pull and an unread pull are each refused with nothing sent, for the lock and for the unlock. A 204 that does not read back as asked is FAILED. A refused write already in the asked state is idempotent. mailbox-open's lock, unlock and canary plans run through the executor.
- `node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --self-test`: 400 cases pass (was 389); the doorbell battery floor is 44 → 55. ⭐ A fleet knock is read and a maintainer's knock is read. ⛔ A drive-by knock, spelled perfectly, reads only the ignored verdict, with the body marker absent from the result. Look-alike or missing authors are ignored, ignored rows are listed apart, the printout names who may ring, and H72 never lists a drive-by row. Round 1 adds: ⭐ the relay's canary reads `canary` (with or without a signature line); ⛔ the same line from a maintainer, with a second line or under `To:` reads as before, and an outsider's is ignored; `mailboxEvents` lists it apart; H72 does not list it.
- `dispatch.mjs` (418), `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` (530) and `post-stamped.mjs` (787) `--self-test` all pass unchanged, and `check-half-states.mjs` and `check-handover.mjs` load.

**Forced test edits (named):** in the recognisers' doorbell battery, the fixture row author `DB_ROW` changed from `os-bill` to the relay's identity, because a knock arrives as the relay's comment. Under the new fence an `os-bill` row is ignored. The one case asserting `by === 'os-bill'` now asserts the relay's login. The H72 end-to-end case is otherwise unchanged and still lists the same three comments. In round 1, two pins changed because the rows changed: the lock's request shape now carries the `mailboxLock` fence descriptor (mailbox-open and validate), and validate's "no unlock row" case became "exactly two ops name a lock". In execute.mjs the row text for an idempotent landing is now taken from the confirming function when it names one (`idempotentText`); the branch delete's text is unchanged.

## Acceptance notes

- The relay App commenting on a locked conversation is still not measured by hand, but no lock this code makes can leave a deaf mailbox: every lock is followed by the canary, and a refused canary takes the lock back. The sweep's first `--lock N` is that measurement. If its canary is refused, the sweep stops there.
- The one-off sweep over every open mailbox is a relay run for the seat after merge (`mailbox-open.mjs --lock N` per open `pm:mailbox` PR). It is not run here. Each lock posts one canary, so each subscribed seat gets one PR-activity event, which its doorbell reader names a canary.
- The relay fence is a label fence: it stops a mistyped or injected number, not a hostile seat, which could add the label first.
- Item 3, what it needs:
  - A reader of the named seat's sessions, from its `pm:seat` post stub (session ID, `Successor-of:`) and its mailbox opening (the body footer's session URL).
  - A predicate over `readSignatureLine` that compares the knock's signature session with that set and reports "unverified seat signature".
  - A consumer that reads it, the receiving seat's knock read. That consumer is a board read, which this PR's pure reader does not do.
- `seat-post-protocol.md` now stands at 87 lines under a ceiling of 88 (headroom 1). The pin lives in `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`, outside this card's file surface, so review nit N2 is not taken here.
- `execute.mjs` joined the file surface in round 1 (claim amendment 6896718263). PR #33975 touches its self-test fixture too; a later lander resolves the conflict.
